A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiMuon research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, revised and relocated material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 Section 5 reports original DistilGPT2/WikiText-103 and ViT/Tiny-ImageNet experiments, including perplexity, accuracy, memory measurements and training curves in Tables 2–3 and Figures 2–4.

after.justification: V3 reports original Mamba-130M/WikiText-103, Qwen2.5-0.5B/MiniPile and ViT/Tiny-ImageNet experiments, including performance, memory, rank comparisons and runtime results in Tables 2–5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The full-rank and compressed STORM recurrences, RSVD compression and parameter updates are retained. V3 Algorithms 3–4 explicitly describe the Newton–Schulz alternative already permitted in v1 Section 3; this expands implementation documentation and theoretical treatment without establishing a new optimizer component.

E1.justification: V3 adds MiniPile, described as a diverse text corpus containing approximately 300 million tokens, for language-model training and evaluation. WikiText-103 and Tiny-ImageNet remain. This substantially expands the represented language data; replacing DistilGPT2 with Mamba on retained WikiText-103 is separately a model-setting change.

E2.justification: Adam is added to the ViT comparison in v3 Table 4 and Figure 4; v1 Table 3 and Figures 3–4 omit it. Adam already appeared in v1's DistilGPT2 curves. AdamW, Lion, SUMO, Muon and Muon++ remain comparators. Gluon is added only to theoretical positioning, not independently evaluated.

E3.justification: The WikiText-103 configuration changes from DistilGPT2 with batch size 8 and sequence length 512 to Mamba-130M with batch size 64 and sequence length 256. ViT batch size changes from 64 to 128, and LiMuon learning rate/beta change from 0.001/0.1 to 0.005/0.05. Qwen introduces a 2,000-iteration, batch-16, sequence-1024 protocol. Top-5 accuracy and timing to target loss 3.70 are new evaluation measures.

E4.justification: V1 compares full-rank LiMuon against one compressed configuration per model. V3 expands this to ranks 4, 8 and 16 across three architectures, probing the accuracy–memory tradeoff. New Table 5 separately examines optimizer-update time and end-to-end time to target loss, adding direct evidence about compression overhead and practical convergence speed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, standard deviations, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both present point estimates and training curves without identified uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: The DistilGPT2 results are removed and new Mamba/Qwen results appear: full-rank LiMuon validation perplexities are 47.78 and 40.83 in v3 Tables 2–3. ViT results are replaced under revised settings: v1 reports 26.59% testing accuracy for Option #1, whereas v3 reports 48.04% validation top-1 accuracy for full-rank LiMuon. These are not same-setting gains. Rank-specific, top-5 and runtime result entries are also added.

T1.justification: V3 Section 4.2 and Appendix B add four Newton–Schulz convergence theorems, nuclear/operator-norm smoothness assumptions and a polar-approximation-error definition. Existing exact-SVD bounds and proofs also change, including tighter dimension dependence. V1's Assumption 5 relating compression error to the true gradient is replaced by a momentum-relative argument in Lemma A.4, with revised rank, oversampling and compression-error conditions.

C1.justification: Beyond v1's exact-SVD convergence claims, v3's abstract, contributions and conclusion newly claim lower sample complexity for LiMuon with Newton–Schulz steps: O(χ_q^3 ε^-3), compared with the cited Muon bound O(χ_q^4 ε^-4). This materially extends the central theoretical contribution while retaining the original objective of combining variance reduction with lower memory.

C2.justification: V3 adds an explanation attributing advantages over Muon++ to avoiding gradient clipping and its tuning parameter. It interprets Mamba and Qwen results as evidence of applicability to state-space models and architectures with grouped-query attention, and discusses the new runtime tradeoffs. The existing explanation that RSVD exchanges additional computation for reduced state memory remains.

D1.justification: New Appendix C Tables 6–9 provide optimizer-specific hyperparameters and search ranges, including clipping thresholds and SUMO update periods. V3 also specifies ten Newton–Schulz steps, Nesterov momentum and explicit Newton–Schulz implementation details. Reported hardware changes from NVIDIA 5090 to A100-SXM4-80GB. V1's explicit ViT cosine-scheduler disclosure is no longer supplied.

R1.justification: V3 substantively revises positioning against Muon++ by explicitly acknowledging its STORM-based variance reduction and emphasizing compression and absence of clipping as distinctions. It adds explicit firstness claims for low-rank STORM and variance-reduced Muon analyses, plus comparisons with Gluon and Kim and Oh's Newton–Schulz analysis. Mamba, MiniPile and Qwen references replace the removed DistilGPT2-related references.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution framing and experimental narratives are extensively rewritten. The convergence discussion is reorganized into exact-SVD and Newton–Schulz branches; supporting lemmas move out of the main text while remaining in the appendix. The former single appendix becomes separate exact-SVD, Newton–Schulz and experimental appendices, substantially changing document organization.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format. Table 1 gains a Newton–Schulz column, and runtime and hyperparameter tables are added. DistilGPT2 plots are replaced by Mamba and Qwen displays. The two original ViT figures are reworked into a six-panel Figure 4 in Appendix C, including new top-5 plots.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses substantial gaps in v1's support for practical efficiency: rank comparisons and wall-clock measurements make the accuracy, memory and computation tradeoffs directly assessable, while Tables 6–9 make experimental tuning much easier to inspect and reproduce. Section 4.2 and Appendix B also provide conditional analysis of the practical orthogonalization previously only mentioned. These gains are substantial despite remaining limitations: uncertainty is still unreported, the theory requires approximation-error conditions, and compressed variants are not uniformly faster.
